# `allocation-size-overflow`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports unchecked runtime multiplication used as an allocation length.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Overflow can allocate less memory than the caller expects, making subsequent
indexed writes unsafe.

## When it fires

It applies to recognized allocation calls whose size argument directly contains
runtime multiplication. The risk is target- and range-dependent: a product that
fits `usize` on a 64-bit target may overflow on a narrower supported target.
When project invariants establish tighter bounds than the types express, use a
focused suppression rather than changing the portable arithmetic check.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn grid(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, w: usize, h: usize) ![]u8 {
    return allocator.alloc(u8, w * h);
}
```
